w: Four kabakas of Buganda lie under a vast thatched dome built from reed and bark cloth - once called one of sub-Saharan Africa's most remarkable buildings, UNESCO-listed since 2001. Fire gutted the tomb-house in 2010; Ugandans crowdfunded the rebuild, brick by brick, until it cleared the 'in danger' list in 2023.
s: Buganda's royal tombs, rebuilt after fire
_facts: Burial site of four kabakas (kings) of Buganda
Traditional architecture built from purely vegetal materials
UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2001
Fire destroyed major buildings in 2010; listed 'in danger' from 2010
Rebuilt via crowdfunding campaign 'Etofaali' plus Japanese government aid, restored by 2023, removed from danger list

w: Muammar Gaddafi bankrolled this mosque as a gift to Uganda's Muslims, its 50.5-metre minaret defining Kampala's skyline since 2006. Officially the Uganda National Mosque now, but still known by its original name - the largest mosque in East Africa, room for some 15,000 worshippers between hall, gallery and courtyard.
s: Gaddafi's gift, East Africa's biggest mosque
_facts: Completed 2006, previously named Gaddafi National Mosque
Commissioned by Muammar Gaddafi as a gift to Uganda
Largest mosque in East Africa; holds ~15,000 plus 1,100 in gallery and 3,500 in the sahn
50.5m minaret defines Kampala's skyline, sits on Kampala Hill in Old Kampala

n: Basilica of the Uganda Martyrs, Namugongo
w: A Latin Catholic minor basilica at Namugongo, dedicated to the Uganda Martyrs - one of Kampala's most significant religious landmarks, even on a record this short: name, dedication, done.
_facts: Latin Catholic minor basilica
Dedicated to the Uganda Martyrs
Located at Namugongo, Kampala

w: Founded in 1908 after the colonial governor called for 'all articles of interest' on Uganda to be handed in, this is the country's oldest museum - playable traditional instruments, hunting gear, weaponry and archaeology packed into one Kampala hall, a century on from that first appeal.
_facts: Founded 1908 after governor George Wilson's call for 'articles of interest'
Displays ethnological, natural-history and traditional-life collections
Collections include playable musical instruments, hunting equipment, weaponry, archaeology and entomology

w: Uganda's oldest Anglican cathedral, seat of the country's first diocese from 1890 and provincial cathedral of the whole Church of Uganda from 1919 to 1967, before the job moved to Nakasero and then quietly moved back. A hilltop institution that has outlasted every reshuffle around it.
_facts: Oldest Anglican cathedral in Uganda
Diocesan cathedral of Namirembe Diocese, founded 1890, first in the province
Served as provincial cathedral of the Church of Uganda 1919-1967
Headquarters later moved to All Saints Nakasero, then back to Namirembe

w: The Buganda Kingdom's parliament sits inside this building - the Lukiiko's chamber, and the working office of both the Kabaka and his prime minister, the Katikkiro. A kingdom operating inside a republic, still running its own affairs from its own royal seat.
_facts: Houses the Lukiiko (Parliament) of the Kingdom of Buganda
Royal Seat of the Buganda Kingdom
Kabaka of Buganda and the Katikkiro (Prime Minister) keep offices here
Administrative headquarters of the Buganda Kingdom

w: Fresh produce, textiles, shoes and cheap electronics, all packed at the foot of Nakasero hill just off Entebbe Road - one of the biggest markets in Kampala's central business district, and still the everyday pulse of the city centre.
s: Kampala's biggest market, foot of the hill
_facts: Located at the foot of Nakasero hill, 50m off Entebbe Road
Sells fresh food, textiles, shoes, cheap electronics
One of the biggest markets in Kampala's central business district

w: Uganda's legal deposit library, established by Act of Parliament in 2003 to replace the old Public Libraries Board - a quiet institution on Buganda Road holding a copy of everything ever legally published in the country.
_facts: Established 2003 by Act of Parliament
Replaced the Public Libraries Board (est. 1964)
Legal deposit library for Uganda
Located on Buganda Road, Kampala
